solutions/founders.title: Research a focused prospect list before writing the pitch.
solutions/founders.sub: Use Scalar to organize companies, inspect contact details and prepare follow-up while you learn who fits your product.
solutions/founders.problem: A long list of unqualified names creates more outreach work without explaining why anyone should care.

steps.title: Define the fit
steps.body: Add your product context and describe a narrow customer problem.

steps.title: Research candidates
steps.body: Discover companies, verify the intended identity and inspect sources.

steps.title: Prepare the next step
steps.body: Save the relevant findings and review a draft against the prospect’s situation.

benefits.title: A reason to reach out
benefits.body: Research gives the message a concrete basis.

benefits.title: One record to revisit
benefits.body: Notes, people and company context remain connected.

benefits.title: Controlled experimentation
benefits.body: Use a small research budget while you test the segment.

solutions/founders.limits: Research does not guarantee buying intent, replies or revenue. Review data accuracy and communication permissions before outreach.

solutions/sales.title: Put the account research beside the next follow-up.
solutions/sales.sub: Give sellers and their agents a CRM record they can inspect, update and use when preparing the next conversation.
solutions/sales.problem: Switching between research tabs, a spreadsheet and a draft can lose the detail that made the account relevant.

steps.title: Choose the account
steps.body: Start from a company domain or verified contact.

steps.title: Fill useful gaps
steps.body: Request the enrichment needed for the next decision and inspect the result.

steps.title: Review the follow-up
steps.body: Use activity history and account context to prepare a relevant message.

benefits.title: More useful preparation
benefits.body: Research stays attached to the account.

benefits.title: Visible next actions
benefits.body: Keep follow-up work in the pipeline instead of a private note.

benefits.title: Fewer blind assumptions
benefits.body: Source checks can expose missing or uncertain data.

solutions/sales.limits: A found address or phone number is not permission to contact someone. Sending requires configured channels and user approval.

solutions/agencies.title: Keep each client’s prospecting context distinct.
solutions/agencies.sub: Use workspace records, segments and explicit research criteria to organize client prospecting work.
solutions/agencies.problem: Reusing the wrong product context or mixing account data can produce an irrelevant pitch and a difficult handoff.

steps.title: Set the boundary
steps.body: Select the correct workspace and confirm who can access it.

steps.title: Define the segment
steps.body: Document the client’s offer, exclusions and target criteria before research.

steps.title: Hand back evidence
steps.body: Review the matching accounts and supporting findings before any campaign action.

benefits.title: A clearer brief
benefits.body: The agent has a specific product and audience to research.

benefits.title: Reviewable lists
benefits.body: A client can understand why an account was selected.

benefits.title: Shared work history
benefits.body: Keep the research trail available for follow-up.

solutions/agencies.limits: Validate workspace access and provider configuration before client use. Team seats and pooled allowances depend on the selected plan.

solutions/agent-builders.title: Give your agent a CRM it can read and update.
solutions/agent-builders.sub: Connect through MCP to supported research and CRM actions, with a visible credit balance for metered work.
solutions/agent-builders.problem: A folder of research files makes it difficult to keep people, companies and next actions consistent.

steps.title: Connect a client
steps.body: Authorize a scoped integration using the documented setup.

steps.title: Read before writing
steps.body: Inspect the current account and verify identity before attaching enrichment.

steps.title: Bound the work
steps.body: Estimate research credits, review results and keep communication actions explicit.

benefits.title: Structured records
benefits.body: The agent operates on people, companies and pipeline data.

benefits.title: Reusable findings
benefits.body: Later tasks can use earlier research.

benefits.title: Visible usage
benefits.body: Metered actions consume the account’s credit allowance.

solutions/agent-builders.limits: MCP access does not imply permission to send messages, buy top-ups or enroll in a plan. Those actions need explicit authorization.

product/autopilot.title: Turn a research goal into a bounded plan.
product/autopilot.sub: Prepare a budgeted autopilot plan, inspect its steps and approve it before execution.
product/autopilot.problem: An open-ended research instruction can consume credits without producing a list you would actually use.

steps.title: Define the goal
steps.body: Describe the desired accounts and the exclusions that matter.

steps.title: Review the plan
steps.body: Inspect the proposed steps and maximum credit budget.

steps.title: Approve and monitor
steps.body: Start only after review, then inspect results or pause the plan.

benefits.title: A visible scope
benefits.body: The plan makes the intended work inspectable.

benefits.title: A budget before execution
benefits.body: Know the proposed allowance before paid research starts.

benefits.title: A place to intervene
benefits.body: Pause and inspect progress when the direction is wrong.

product/autopilot.limits: Budgeted research does not guarantee qualified prospects or a business outcome. Provider results still need identity and relevance checks.

product/pipeline.title: Keep research connected to the next conversation.
product/pipeline.sub: Organize contacts, companies, activity and deal stages in the same CRM.
product/pipeline.problem: Research loses value when the account record has no clear next step.

steps.title: Review the account
steps.body: Check company identity and the supporting information.

steps.title: Set the next action
steps.body: Record the follow-up, owner and relevant stage.

steps.title: Update from the result
steps.body: Keep activity current after a conversation or decision.

benefits.title: Continuity for follow-up
benefits.body: The next person can see what already happened.

benefits.title: A visible pipeline
benefits.body: Stages help organize the work still ahead.

benefits.title: Context for agents
benefits.body: Supported tools can retrieve the current account before preparing a draft.

product/pipeline.limits: A stage is a workflow state, not verified revenue. Outcomes depend on the quality of the offer and the customer’s choice.

resources/first-research.title: Run one research task you can check.
resources/first-research.sub: Start with a known company and a small question before asking an agent to build a large list.
resources/first-research.problem: A broad discovery run is difficult to evaluate if you have not tested identity matching and credit usage.

steps.title: Choose a known account
steps.body: Use its domain and an unambiguous company name.

steps.title: Request one useful fact
steps.body: Estimate the credit charge and inspect the returned source.

steps.title: Check the record
steps.body: Confirm the result is attached to the correct company before expanding the run.

benefits.title: A clear first success
benefits.body: You can judge accuracy against a known account.

benefits.title: A bounded spend
benefits.body: One task makes it easier to understand usage.

benefits.title: A safer repeatable process
benefits.body: Carry the identity check into larger research tasks.

resources/first-research.limits: An unverified match should remain missing. Do not accept a same-name stranger just to fill a field.

resources/credit-guide.title: Budget the research steps, not just the final list.
resources/credit-guide.sub: Credits measure priced actions. A single prospect can require several searches and enrichment steps.
resources/credit-guide.problem: A claim that a plan buys a fixed number of leads hides differences in research depth and provider results.

steps.title: Choose the actions
steps.body: List discovery, email lookup, company enrichment and other required steps.

steps.title: Multiply by the workload
steps.body: Use the published per-action schedule and include planned repeats.

steps.title: Set a stopping point
steps.body: Review the credit balance and any autopilot budget before increasing the workload.

benefits.title: A clearer estimate
benefits.body: The calculation reflects the actual work requested.

benefits.title: Visible tradeoffs
benefits.body: Choose which missing facts justify another paid action.

benefits.title: No promised lead count
benefits.body: A credit allowance is not a guarantee of contacts or sales.

resources/credit-guide.limits: Current action examples: web search 2 credits, email lookup 8, company discovery 12, company aspect 30. Provider-backed agent turns may have additional charges. Check billing before buying.

resources/review-before-outreach.title: Review the person, the evidence and the message.
resources/review-before-outreach.sub: Use research to prepare a relevant follow-up without treating an AI draft as permission to send.
resources/review-before-outreach.problem: The wrong identity or an unsupported claim can damage a conversation before it begins.

steps.title: Confirm identity
steps.body: Match the person with the intended company or domain.

steps.title: Check the claim
steps.body: Open supporting sources and remove uncertain personalizations.

steps.title: Approve the action
steps.body: Check sender, recipients, channel permissions and final wording before sending.

benefits.title: Fewer wrong attachments
benefits.body: Identity comes before enrichment.

benefits.title: A more relevant draft
benefits.body: The message uses facts you can defend.

benefits.title: A deliberate decision
benefits.body: You choose whether the communication is appropriate.

resources/review-before-outreach.limits: This checklist is workflow guidance, not a guarantee of deliverability or regulatory compliance.
